content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (TB) treatment, specifically for drug-resistant TB, were updated in 2022. These guidelines include recommendations for the use of shorter, all-oral regimens for multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB) and pre-extensively drug-resistant TB (pre-XDR-TB). 2. A six-month regimen consisting of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL) was evaluated for its efficacy and safety in patients with pulmonary pre-XDR-TB (MDR/RR-TB with fluoroquinolone-susceptible disease). This regimen was compared to longer, bedaquiline-containing oral regimens lasting 9–12 months. 3. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the treatment success of the BPaL regimen compared to WHO-recommended shorter and longer regimens. These analyses included adjustments for variables such as age, sex, HIV status, prior TB history, smear status, and antiretroviral therapy (ART) use among HIV-positive individuals. 4. Observational studies used to evaluate the BPaL regimen were noted to have significant limitations, including a high risk of bias, small sample sizes, and potential confounding factors. These limitations led to downgrading the quality of evidence to very low in some cases. 5. The Zenix trial, which evaluated the BPaL regimen, was conducted in settings that may not be directly comparable to programmatic settings. Despite this, the certainty of evidence was not downgraded for indirectness. 6. The BPaL regimen demonstrated increased treatment success rates across all subgroups, reduced mortality, and reduced loss to follow-up. However, it was associated with an increase in grade 3 or higher adverse events. There was no significant difference in the development of amplified drug resistance. 7. The TB-PRACTECAL trial, a multi-site, multi-arm, open-label, phase II/III randomized controlled trial, was conducted in Uzbekistan, South Africa, and Belarus. It was implemented by Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine. The trial aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of bedaquilineand pretomanid-containing regimens compared to the local standard of care (SOC) regimen. 8. The TB-PRACTECAL trial was terminated early in March 2021 after the Data and Safety Monitoring Board found that the investigational regimen was superior to the SOC in terms of safety and efficacy. 9. Eligibility criteria for the TB-PRACTECAL trial included patients with culture-positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to at least rifampicin, confirmed by molecular or phenotypic drug susceptibility testing. Exclusion criteria included known allergies to study drugs, pregnancy, QT prolongation, significant cardiac history, and prior use of bedaquiline, pretomanid, or linezolid for more than one month. 10. The modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population for the trial included all randomized patients who received at least one dose of the study medication and had culture-positive TB resistant to rifampicin. 11. The investigational regimens in the TB-PRACTECAL trial included combinations of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and either moxifloxacin (BPaLM) or clofazimine (BPaLC) for 24 weeks. 12. The WHO guidelines recommend the use of shorter, all-oral regimens for MDR/RR-TB, including the BPaL regimen, based on evidence from trials like TB-PRACTECAL. These regimens are designed to improve treatment outcomes while minimizing adverse events and the duration of therapy.
